draft.title: Knights, castles and chivalry
card: Knights
Knights were warriors who fought on horseback for a lord. They trained for years, often starting as boys, to learn to ride, use weapons and wear heavy armour.
Chivalry
Chivalry was a code of conduct for knights. It called for loyalty to their lord, courage in battle and protection of the weak. Knights did not always live up to it.
Castles
Castles were strong homes for lords. Thick walls, towers and often a moat made them hard to attack, so they protected the lord, his family and his people.
A castle also showed the lord's power. Its size and position let it overlook the land around it, which reminded everyone nearby who ruled there.
draft.remember: Knights fought by a code of chivalry, and castles both defended a lord and showed his power.

a.q: What was chivalry in medieval Europe?
opts: A code of conduct that knights were expected to follow
A set of laws made by the king for all peasants
A type of armour worn by knights on horseback
The training a boy had to finish to become a knight
a.why: Chivalry was a code for how knights should behave, with loyalty, courage and protection of the weak. Training is tempting, but that was how knights learned to fight, not the code they were meant to follow.
a.clue: Think about how a knight was meant to behave, not how he fought.

b.q: Lord Edmund builds a tall stone castle on a hill above the villages he rules. Besides defence, what does the castle's size and position do?
opts: Shows his power over the land around it
Lets his peasants leave the manor safely
Trains his knights in the code of chivalry
Collects a share of the villagers' crops
b.why: A large castle on a hill can be seen from the villages, so it shows the lord's power over the land around. Defence is also a purpose, but the question asks for what else it did. Training knights was done by other means, not by the building's size.
b.clue: Who could see the castle from the villages below?

a.best: A code of conduct that knights were expected to follow

b.best: Shows his power over the land around it

problems.detail: 'Knights fought by a code of chivalry' suggests knights actually followed the code. The card says chivalry was a code they were expected to follow but 'did not always live up to'. Wording such as 'Knights were expected to follow a code of chivalry' would match the card.

check.summary: The facts and both questions are sound, and each question has one clearly right answer. One minor issue: the remember line says knights 'fought by' the code of chivalry, which glosses over the card's point that they did not always live up to it.
